sections.h2: What should a Coral Gables seller know before choosing how to sell?
sections.html:
Gables homeowners generally choose among a broker listing, a do-it-yourself sale, and an as-is offer from a buyer with cash. Your timeline and the house's condition drive the choice.

The city calls itself the "City Beautiful," and the city's own site says more than 1,000 properties sit on the Coral Gables Register of Historic Places. Check with the city before promising a buyer any renovation if your address is on that register. At $2,373 a month, typical rent is high enough that some owners think about renting the house out instead.

sections.h2: How big is Coral Gables and who lives there?
sections.html:
Coral Gables is a Miami-Dade County city of 49,578 people as of the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, on 12.93 square miles of land. Census recorded 3,809.7 residents for each of those square miles in 2020.

Pricing a sale starts with these local numbers.

sections.h2: What does the local economy mean for a Coral Gables home sale?
sections.html:
Employers and institutions support a steady pool of buyers who relocate for work. The city lists more than 20 consulates and foreign government offices and more than 140 multinational corporations within its limits.

  • Shops in the city rang up $2,590,246 thousand in 2022 sales, per Census, a retail figure of $53,325 per resident.
  • Workers here spend 23.8 minutes getting to a job, against 26.4 nationally.
  • A four-year degree or more is held by 73.6% of adults over 25.

Buyers from outside the area often want a clean title file and quick closing, so sellers who have paperwork ready tend to avoid delays.

sections.h2: What permits and city rules affect selling in Coral Gables?
sections.html:
Start with the city's permits page, which lists every permit the city issues, and its City Services Directory for anything you cannot find. Ask the building staff whether any permit tied to your address is still open before a buyer's title agent asks.

The Development and City Projects page tracks traffic calming and large construction, so check it for work near your block. Meeting agendas and public notices are posted under City Meetings.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when a Coral Gables house is sold?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade's deed tax is 60 cents per $100, with a 45 cents per $100 surtax that does not reach a single-family-only transfer. The base rate sits in s. 201.02, and the Revenue Department says all signers share liability.

  • The clerk takes payment when the deed is filed.
  • Section 28.24 sets page fees of $5.00 and $4.00, with extra trust fund and technology charges.
  • Section 689.01 calls for two witnesses on the deed.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when a Coral Gables home sells?
sections.html:
A buyer of a long-held Coral Gables homestead may owe far more than you did, because the sale lifts assessed value to just value.

  • Save Our Homes holds growth to whichever is lower, 3 percent or inflation.
  • Homestead cuts up to $50,000 from taxable value; claim it by March 1.
  • Renting the house out ends it.

The Miami-Dade appraiser does not mail bills; the tax collector does, with a discount that starts at 4 percent for November payment. The 2026 roll was certified on October 16, 2026. Assessment questions go to the appraiser's public line at 305-375-4712.

sections.h2: What if the house has a mortgage default, a tenant or an estate?
sections.html:
Each situation has its own clock. A court-ordered foreclosure auction falls 20 to 35 days after final judgment. The Revenue Department lists a probate representative's deed as non-taxable.

  • Estates of $150,000 or less in non-exempt property may use summary administration under s. 735.201.
  • Section 83.57 requires 30 days' notice to end a monthly tenancy.
  • Unpaid rent starts with a 3-day written demand.

The Clerk of Court runs a free alert that flags any deed or mortgage recorded under your name, handy for empty or inherited homes.

sections.h2: What steps does a Coral Gables sale follow after you accept an offer?
sections.html:
The deed is written, witnessed twice and recorded by the Miami-Dade clerk. Remote witnessing by audio-video is allowed, so a seller living elsewhere can still sign.

  • Gather mortgage payoff information and any open permit records.
  • Confirm whether your homestead ends with the sale.
  • Ask the title agent how the year's tax bill will be divided.
  • Keep a copy of the recorded deed.

Sellers buying another Florida home can file the portability form with the new homestead application.

sections.h2: Who are the neighbors and buyers in Coral Gables?
sections.html:
In Coral Gables, 56.6% of residents are Hispanic or Latino and 37.7% were born abroad. Census adds that 60.7% of residents aged five and up use another language at home. Sellers who deal with out-of-town or overseas heirs and buyers should expect to work across languages, and a translated summary of the sale terms can prevent confusion at the table.

The city's own description points the same way: consulates, foreign government offices and multinational companies, plus six international sister cities. About 80.7% of residents had not moved in the prior year.

sections.h2: What does life in the City Beautiful offer a buyer?
sections.html:
The city's home page lists a community calendar with art events, a recycling drive-thru, a vintage market at the Merrick House and bike tours, and it notes Giralda Plaza as a gathering spot. A new flag installation there and a first Salute to Veterans were announced in November 2026. The Granada Golf Course is getting rain shelters.

The city marked its centennial in 2025 and runs a smart city platform with open data, maps and sensors. None of this changes a legal step in your sale, yet buyers often ask what the neighborhood feels like, and these pages give you something factual to point to.

sections.h2: Do veteran or senior owners in Coral Gables have special steps?
sections.html:
Census counts 1,041 veterans and finds 18.9% of residents at 65 or older. Veteran and older-owner benefits tie to the homestead, so a sale ends them for that house.

  • The Miami-Dade appraiser lets owners file widow and veteran disability exemptions online.
  • A veteran past 65 with a lasting service-connected disability may get a homestead discount matching the VA rating.
  • Deferral requests go to the tax collector by March 31.

If you hold one of these benefits, ask the appraiser what happens to it at closing and whether you can use it on the next home.

faqs.q: How much is a typical Coral Gables house worth?
faqs.a: Census reports $1,089,900 as the middle value for 2020-2024. Your own house could land on either side of it.

faqs.q: Does a historic designation affect my sale?
faqs.a: It can. Yes, if the house is on the city's historic register. Ask city staff about your address.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamp tax on a Coral Gables deed?
faqs.a: Whoever the contract names, all parties to the deed share liability. The surtax skips a document moving only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: Will my property taxes follow me to a new home?
faqs.a: They can partly. Partly. Portability can move homestead savings to a new home if you qualify, using Form DR-501T.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about my assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Miami-Dade appraiser's public line at 305-375-4712.
